issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for 'numberOfInscribedStudents': the problem statement's UML declares numberOfInscribedStudents as int, but the solution implementation declares it as long. This inconsistency is structural (type difference) and will confuse students about the expected type and how to implement related methods/getters/setters. It also introduces a type mismatch with other parts of the specification that expect int values.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the type of numberOfInscribedStudents consistent across artifacts. Recommended: change the solution's declaration from 'long numberOfInscribedStudents' to 'int numberOfInscribedStudents' and update the corresponding getter/setter signatures to return/take int. Alternatively, if very large values are required, update the UML and all method signatures (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents) to use long consistently; pick one approach and apply it everywhere.

issues.description: Return type / usage mismatch for getTotalNumberOfStudents(): the UML and task expect getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return an int, and the solution method signature returns int, but the solution implementation adds a long field (numberOfInscribedStudents) to an int field (numberOfGuestStudents) and returns the result without an explicit cast. This produces a type inconsistency (long result being returned as int) and will cause compilation errors or require implicit narrowing, which is unintended.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolve the root cause by aligning types: either change numberOfInscribedStudents to int (so the sum is int and can be returned as int) or change the getTotalNumberOfStudents() return type to long (and update the UML and task text accordingly). Ensure the implementation returns the declared type (add explicit cast only if intentionally narrowing and documented).
